lines.text: Writing is only five thousand years old. So where did information live before that?
Inside living bodies. And I mean that directly: a body was the storage.
Bodies carried information two ways. In the body itself — and in behavior.
First, in the body. A coat of spots hides an animal from a lion. That pattern is information — how to stay alive. When the animal had young, the pattern was copied into a new body.
Second, in behavior. A calf learns the way to the water by following its mother. No gene carries that route. It is copied by watching, and by walking it, again and again.
Two kinds of information. One copied by birth. One copied by watching.
Copy after copy, both survived for millions of years.
But there was one fatal rule: die before you pass it on — before you have young, before the young have watched you — and your information dies with you. There was no backup.
Before there were books, information lived in bodies — and it could die with them.
The first archive on Earth was not paper or stone. It was a living body — and the copying was having children, and watching, and learning.
This is only the first chapter of how information evolved on Earth. The story goes on from here — subscribe to Earth One, and take the rest of the walk with us.
